# Prove the AI test entry stays out of production artifacts

Part of #20370 (linked natively); graduated from D#18775 (OQ2 / OQ4 production-artifact contract, STEP_BACK point 6). Blocked by the seam leaf.

## Context

A test entry into the AI write path must never reach a production boot. D#18775 withdrew the blanket "byte-identical build" promise, because a new `DefaultConfig` key changes emitted bytes even while dormant, and replaced it with three checkable claims. This leaf makes them a check.

## The Architectural Reality

- `buildScripts/util/check-consumer-runtime-build.mjs` already builds the Data, Canvas and App workers and Main from an installed copy of the package: the nearest existing guard to extend.
- A file in `src/main/addon/` ships as a lazy chunk in every dist build, which is why the harness half lives in the test tree.

## The Fix

Extend the existing build guard, or add a sibling check beside it, so CI fails when any of the three claims below breaks.

## Discussion Criteria Mapping & Leaf Slice

OQ2's amended production-artifact contract and STEP_BACK point 6. The touchpoints it guards are the epic's `production-touchpoints` inventory.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The harness adapter and the test entry's harness side are absent from the production artifacts the guard builds.
- [ ] A boot without the test flag exposes no dispatch route the pre-change build lacked, checked by enumerating the App Worker's remote methods before and after.
- [ ] `useAiClient` behaviour is unchanged (the seam leaf's specs, referenced, not duplicated).
- [ ] Any byte-parity claim names its before/after artifact pair; otherwise none is made.
- [ ] The check runs in CI and fails on a deliberate leak (a negative control in the PR).

## Out of Scope

The seam itself, the adapter, and the spec suite.
